messages:
mike_support: FYI - customer acme-corp reporting wrong tool_result association when using parallel tool calls. Weather and stock tool outputs swapped intermittently. Request id: rq_01H3ZQ. Happened via JS SDK 1.1.0. Posting payload + response they sent for repro.

jess_prod: Do we have raw request/response logs? Model, endpoint, SDK version?

mike_support: Model: rwd-3b, endpoint: /v1/respond, SDK: @redwood/sdk-js 1.1.0. Logs attached in their message but pasted minimal payload below. No HTTP errors, just content mismatch.

mike_support: ```json
POST /v1/respond
{
  "input": "Get both weather and stock",
  "tools": [
    {"name": "get_weather", "args": "{\"location\": \"NYC\"}"},
    {"name": "get_stock", "args": {"symbol": "AAPL"}}
  ],
  "parallel": true
}
```

mike_support: Customer says response body contained tool_results but mapping looked like:
```json
"tool_results": [
  {"tool_name": "get_weather", "output": "Price: $172"},
  {"tool_name": "get_stock", "output": "Sunny, 60F"}
]
```

sam_eng: Hmm. Looks like their `get_weather` args were stringified (they passed a JSON string) while `get_stock` was an object. That can cause our serializer to treat the first tool payload as literal string and our internal call queue may rehydrate incorrectly. Could be a bug in parallel demux: we use positional mapping of results to tools and rely on stable ordering. If one tool got internal validation error and retried, ordering could shift.

sam_eng: Can you share response headers and whether any tool returned a 400 for schema validation? Also share the full response body (we need the correlation ids).

mike_support: Customer pasted response body, snippet: 
```json
{
  "request_id": "rq_01H3ZQ",
  "tool_results": [
    {"id": "tr_9a", "tool_name": "get_weather", "output": "Price: $172"},
    {"id": "tr_9b", "tool_name": "get_stock", "output": "Sunny, 60F"}
  ],
  "tool_call_map": ["get_weather","get_stock"]
}
```

mike_support: No 4xx shown in their copy. They said it only happens when `parallel=true` and with mixed arg types.

tina_oncall: Assigning to eng-oncall. Sam, can you try a minimal repro with same SDK version and `parallel: true`? If this is a mapping race, we should confirm: do we attach per-tool correlation ids on internal queued calls?

sam_eng: I reproduced locally within 10s. Minimal repro: call SDK with two tools, one arg is stringified, other is object, parallel true. Internal curl to runtime shows: 
```
# internal payloads sent to tools (order may vary)
[
  {"call_id": "c1", "tool": "get_stock", "args": {"symbol":"AAPL"}},
  {"call_id": "c2", "tool": "get_weather", "args": "{\\\"location\\\": \\\"NYC\\\"}"}
]
# runtime responses returned: c1 then c2
# but our demux used original index order to map outputs -> tools, which assumes no reordering.
```

sam_eng: Root cause: we rely on array index stable ordering to map results back to original tool entries. When internal subsystem sorts/queues calls, responses can come back in different order; and because one tool's args were a string, our validation path returns early and triggers a retry, shifting indices.

sam_eng: Temporary mitigation: update SDK to coerce tool args to objects (don't allow pre-stringified), and server-side: change demux to use explicit per-call correlation id (call_id) returned by runtime rather than positional index. I'll open a hotfix PR to add correlation ids and a guard for mixed arg types in the serializer.

jess_prod: Customer is P1 on escalation. Can we give ETA for hotfix + recommended workaround for them?

sam_eng: Workaround: make both tool args full objects (not pre-stringified) or set `parallel:false` for the call. Hotfix plan: 1) server patch to map by call_id (canary) - 6 hours, 2) SDK validation patch - 3 hours, 3) full rollout - next day.

mike_support: OK. I'll share workaround and ask them to set parallel:false until we push canary. Also requested permission for canary rollout.

issue-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045 - tool-result-assoc-mismatch. Priority: P1.

tina_oncall: Thanks team. Sam, please add unit tests for mixed arg types and a regression test for result ordering. Leave a note in the incident with PR links.

mike_support: Thanks — forwarding update to customer and will CC eng on reply. :thumbsup:
